html:
The Djargurd Wurrung were an Aboriginal Australian people of the volcanic plains of southwest Victoria, west of Lake Corangamite. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Their country of grassland, lakes and old volcanic cones was among the first in Victoria to be taken for sheep runs, from the late 1830s. Little is recorded of them in detail. Neighbours on the map include the Gulidjan, the Girai Wurrung and the Gunditjmara, who shared a similar way of life built on eels, waterbirds and the yam daisy. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
